 Screen t2 curates an autumnal K-drama watchlist for your reflective and nostalgic golden hours 
 By Ankita Chandra 
 Published: 31 Oct 2026, 12:00AM | 5 min read You and Everything Else
 Advertisement A year wrapping up its memories, verdant scenes starting to embrace a solemn, muted palette, and the first telltale chills of the sweater weather — autumn’s liminality is often a call for inner reflection. The season’s delicate golden skies and soothing earth tones also create the perfect ambience for resurrecting nostalgic memories, and pausing for a layover of self-reflection. For K-drama enthusiasts, the season often becomes an excuse to go back to timeless love stories like Goblin or journeys of self-discovery like Coffee Prince . But if you have been rewatching the same autumnal stories over and over again, it is high time to revamp your watchlist for the season with some new entries in the genre. Here is a t2 -curated list of five recent K-dramas that evoke all the nostalgic, romantic, reflective and sweetly melancholic notes of autumn.
 Four Hands Two Sonatas 
 Where to watch : Netflix
 Cast : Song Kang, Lee Jun-young, Jang Gyu-ri
 Plot : A musical saga par excellence, Four Hands Two Sonatas is the perfect binge for those days when the slanting sunbeams and cool breezes make you reminisce about everything you have loved and lost in your journey from adolescence to maturity. Two schoolmates, Kang Pi-o (Song Kang) and Choi Jeong-yo (Lee Jun-young) strike a deep brotherhood when they find that their musical talent blooms when they perform together on stage. However, Pi-o’s mother develops insecurity when she discovers that Jeong-yo’s raw passion can easily overshadow Pi-o’s stringent adherence to method, and brews bitterness between them. How the two friends bring back their innocent teenage dynamic while navigating the responsibilities of adulthood as professional musicians becomes the focus of the series. 
 When Life Gives You Tangerines 
 Where to watch: Netflix
 Cast : IU, Park Bo-gum
 Plot : A story that perfectly aligns with the sweet melancholy and liminal tranquility of autumn, When Life Gives You Tangerines depicts love from all its realistic angles. Ae-sun (IU) and Gwan-sik (Bo-gum) brave economic hardships, familial disjunctions and personal failures through an epic love that transcends life’s vicissitudes, across generations. Beyond the love story, the series also highlights the sacrifices made by family members for each other, and how self-definition is inevitably influenced by the aspirations and scars we inherit from our ancestors. Spanning a multi-generational setting right from 1950s till 2025 and unfolding across defining timelines like the 1997 economic crisis in Korea, the story charts the journey of an aspiring poet, her devoted husband and their daughter. Through arguments, emotional di stance and generational wounds, the family builds and rebuilds itself through an intense tale of love, loss and sacrifice. 
 A Love Other than Yours 
 Where to watch: Prime Video
 Cast : Seo Kang-joon, Ahn Eun-jin, Hyeyeon, Lee Joo-ahn
 Plot : Autumn can make heartbreaks linger a little while longer, and  A Love Other than Yours is a series that offers ample catharsis. The plot quite bravely illuminates an aspect of long-term partnerships we often do not like to explore: the fading of passion with the passage of time, when the deepest of our equations can turn into mere habit. Namgung (Seo Kang-joon) is the “green flag” boyfriend many would dream of. Apart from working hard at his job to financially support his struggling girlfriend Mido (Ahn Eun-jin), who is a director, he also takes care of her mental and physical well-being. But to Mido, Namgung spoiling her is a constant reminder of her own inability to achieve the things he has already accomplished in life. She also fears that his indulgence may actually kill her ambition and make her settle comfortably as a failure. When the two call it quits and meet new romantic interests, they realise that the habit of a decade-long relationship is not easy to discard.  A Love Other than Yours is a story that makes you revisit every reluctant goodbye in life, as you bid farewell to another year’s warmth and prepare to welcome the chilly months. 
 You and Everything Else 
 Where to watch: Netflix
 Cast : Kim Go-eun, Park Ji-hyun, Kim Gun-woo
 Plot : If the delicate, flame-hued skies of the autumnal afternoons make you reminisce about the enduring childhood friendships that faded with rising responsibilities in adulthood, this is the perfect watch. Goblin star Kim Go-eun enters her Eun-tak element once again in this series as Eun-jung, a girl who was raised by her struggling mother after her father died during a car accident. Eun-jung’s dull and lonely life begins to look up when she meets Sang-yeon (Ji-hyun), the daughter of a wealthy couple, who becomes Eun-jung’s best friend. Sang-yeon’s family takes care of Eun-jung like its own member, and Eun-jung starts to gradually fall for her friend’s elder brother. When he also passes away and Sang-yeon’s family goes bankrupt, the friendship between the two gets swallowed up by life’s c hallenges. When they meet in college, they end up falling for the same person, further complicating the dynamic. Years later, Eun-jung again crosses paths with her long-lost friend, who is now suffering from a terminal illness, and does not have much time left. A poignant story of two soul sisters who barely get time to reconcile after years of shifting equations, You and Everything Else will surely make you pick up the phone and reconnect with your childhood friends by the time you finish the final episode. 
 Can This Love Be Translated? 
 Where to watch: Netflix
 Cast : Kim Seon-ho, Go Youn-jung, Sota Fukushi
 Plot : A story where travel becomes a medium of self-discovery, and a strangers-to-lovers dynamic leads to healing for both the protagonists, Can This Love Be Translated? is the ultimate autumnal daydream to relish slowly as you snuggle up to the transitioning season’s cosy, temperate warmth. Moo-hee (Go Youn-jung) is a rising actor who bumps into Ho-jin (Kim Seon-ho), a multilingual interpreter during her time in Japan, and sparks fly almost instantly. Although the two do not realise it instantly, the plot gives a clear message for the audience to presume that the two protagonists are fated soulmates. While Ho-jin lives his life translating and conveying others’ feelings while keeping his own inner world at bay, Moo-hee struggles with childhood trauma and dreadful hallucinations, with no one to u nderstand or comfort her. When the two work together on a reality travel show, they come closer and finally shed their vulnerabilities as their hearts are finally “translated” to each other.
